title: Jacobi fields, conjugate points and comparison
summary: Variations through geodesics (Definition 9.1); the Jacobi equation ∇_X∇_X J + R(J,X)X = 0 (Definition 9.3) and existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields (Proposition 9.5); Jacobi fields in constant curvature and on the sphere (Examples 9.11–9.13); conjugate points and the differential of the exponential map; the distance comparison with a constant-curvature model (Theorem 9.18).

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is Gudmundsson chapter 9 (Definitions 9.1, 9.3; Propositions 9.2, 9.5; Examples 9.10–9.16; Lemma 9.17; Theorem 9.18) with Wendl §6.4 and Lee chapters 10–11 as the commercial reference.

preparation.description: Read Gudmundsson chapter 9, pp. 125–127: Definition 9.1 (variations of geodesics), Proposition 9.2, Definition 9.3 (Jacobi fields), Example 9.4, Proposition 9.5.
Read pp. 128–135: Jacobi fields in the plane, the sphere and the hyperbolic disc (Examples 9.10–9.13), Example 9.16 and Lemma 9.17, Theorem 9.18 (distance comparison).
Open-licensed alternative: Wendl §6.4 (geodesics, arc length and sectional curvature).
